Open domain question answering is a longstanding task in natural language processing that can answer factoid questions, from a large knowledge corpus such as Wikipedia or BookCorpus.
outputs: The paper focuses on generating direct answers to open-domain factoid questions, often through retrieval-augmented or generative methods.

quote: Exact match (EM) scores on Natural Questions and TriviaQA datasets indicate answering quality
Exact match (EM) scores on Natural Questions and TriviaQA datasets indicate answering quality.

In terms of answering quality, EM (Exact Match accuracy), F1-score, MRR@k (Mean Reciprocal Rank), precision@k, Recall@k and retrieval accuarcy@k are normally used to measure the quality of the ODQA models. Specifically, EM is the percentage of questions for which the predicted answers can match any one of the reference answers exactly, after string normalization.
